requirement:
Setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions MUST
explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose
justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` and author or refresh
its citation review using `habeas author`. The instructions MUST explain that
the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration,
that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception, and that
ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its
target.
rationale:
The subject requires two things: setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions must each explain five points. The five points are: (1) how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose justification; (2) authoring or refreshing its citation review with `habeas author`; (3) that the anchor needs no project declaration or exception-specific configuration; (4) that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception; and (5) that ordinary partly covered functions need no exception when their file meets its target.

**Generated coverage documentation.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` builds the coverage chapter through `populate_in`. It runs for two section-number variants and asserts that the generated chapter content contains each of these phrases:
- `habeas:coverage` (point 1)
- `substantive prose justification` (point 1)
- `fenced commentary or a Rust doc comment` (point 1)
- `citation review with \`habeas author\`` (point 2)
- `No project declaration or special configuration` (point 3)
- `current accepted review` (point 4)
- `Ordinary partly covered functions\nneed no exception when their file meets its target` (point 5)

The test checks the rendered chapter, not just the source constant `GUIDANCE`. That constant does contain this text.

**Bundled agent instructions.** `tests/repository.rs#fn[shared_agent_guidance_documents_post_suite_checks_and_standard_explanations]` reads `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` and asserts the following phrases:
- the standard `{cite}` of `habeas:coverage` (point 1)
- the rationale in fenced commentary or a Rust doc comment (point 1)
- the citation review with `habeas author` (point 2)
- "Only current accepted review evidence permits the exception" (point 4)
- "No project declaration or extra configuration is needed" (point 3)
- "Partly covered functions need no exception when their file meets its target" (point 5)

**Other test.** `tests/setup.rs#fn[coverage_setup_is_idempotent_and_hook_needs_no_coverage_chapter]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject but only checks setup idempotence. It adds nothing for this requirement, but the two tests above cover every obligation, so this is not a gap.

**Remaining uncertainty.** Other skill files mention `habeas:coverage` (`habeas-evidence`, `habeas-requirements`, and the references under `habeas`). The tests do not assert their text. I read the requirement as satisfied by the main agent instructions, which carry the full explanation. The other files point to it. I treat this as a reasonable reading, not an adequacy gap.

The tests exercise each explanation obligation with assertions on the actual text, so I found no gap.

Setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions MUST
explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose
justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` and author or refresh
its citation review using `habeas author`. The instructions MUST explain that
the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration,
that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception, and that
ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its
target.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
